directions.title: Does a correctly scheduled noise model close the Stage 1 gap?
directions.assumption_at_stake: The Stage 1 gap is the device departing from its calibration, not our simulator mis-built
directions.cheapest_test: Re-simulate the archived ISA circuit ALAP-scheduled (FakeFez durations) with job-time calibration; pass if P(yes) >= 0.40
directions.rules_out: Rules out our simulator's missing idle decay as the cause of the 3 November gap: scheduling the circuit correctly moved the prediction by about 0.000 (0.268 against 0.267).
directions.prior_work_line: Vezvaee et al. 2025 (arXiv:2510.18847, Heron r2) found calibration-derived noise models must be scaled 2.3 to 4.0 times to match deep circuits, and Bautra et al. 2026 (arXiv:2603.14607, Eagle) found from_backend twins matched hardware at 95% in only 7 of 96 cases. So a correctly scheduled calibration model is predicted to stay far below the chip's 0.50: fail. Settled bet ng-p3-1: 0.268, fail.
prior_work_sources: Vezvaee et al. 2025, surface-code scaling on Heron versus calibration noise models (descriptor per reads D), arXiv:2510.18847

directions.title: Is there a one-friend genuine LF inequality?

directions.title: Do both error terms show up again when the three entangled pairs are measured in a fresh chip job?
directions.assumption_at_stake: P3-5c's 'both terms on every pair' describes the chip, not one afternoon's job.
directions.cheapest_test: One new job: program 1's three witness circuits on their original qubits, 9 tomography settings x 2,000 shots each, plus readout calibration; P3-5c's fits, unchanged.
directions.models: none: the chip is the referee, no model (rule 12 does not apply)
directions.odds_event: On the fresh job, the 16-knob model needs both the rotation-type and the blur-type term (each p < 0.01) on at least 2 of the 3 pairs.
directions.odds_rationale: Invariant 7: P3-5c is pass-unreplicated. Both kinds of error are generic on superconducting chips, so a second job should need both; but half the shots widen the nulls, calibration drifts between days (P3-15's runs), and h221's rotation label was the weakest. Above the running base rate 8/19 = 0.42 (ledger/brier.md).
directions.question: If we measure the same entangled qubit pairs again on a new day, do both kinds of error show up again?
known: On 3 November's data, all three pairs needed both a 'rotation' and a 'blur' error term.
That was one job on one afternoon; the chip's behaviour has shifted between runs before.
directions.human_prompt: Would you spend about 18 seconds of chip time to measure the same three entangled qubit pairs again on a new day and see whether both kinds of error show up again? Will it come back a hit (here, a hit means both show up on at least two of the three pairs)?
engine_only: all 3 of 3 pairs again: engine odds 0.40 (correlated)
directions.odds_template: remap one pass (operators/remap.md), not v1; re-elicit under v1 before pre-registration
directions.prior_work_line: Vezvaee et al. 2025 (arXiv:2510.18847, Heron r2) report both coherent CZ error and non-Markovian dephasing, and Cenedese et al. 2023 (arXiv:2211.16114, ibm_lagos) a coherent rotation on top of decay, so a fresh job is predicted to need both terms: pass. Drift as in Kim et al. 2025 (arXiv:2407.02467, T1 over 300% in 60 h) could change which pair carries which term. ng-p3-5c found both on 3 of 3 pairs, unreplicated.

questions_closed.question: Why did program 1's circuit read 0.502 on the chip on the afternoon of 3 November, against about 0.26 predicted?
questions_closed.diagnosis: In every run since (4 and 5 November), putting back the barrier, changing how the shots were grouped, and running the circuit alone in its own job each left the chip at about 30% 'yes', and a better-built simulator did not explain the gap either, so we ruled those out; we could not rule out that the chip itself was different that afternoon (its calibration, drift, or something IBM's servers did that day), because that afternoon cannot be run again.
questions_closed.reopen_if: a later run of this circuit comes back near 0.50 under any condition
